examples.ko: 두꺼운 겨울옷은 옷장 맨 위 칸에 있어요.
examples.en: The thick winter clothes are on the top shelf of the closet.

examples.ko: 지금 겨울옷을 세일해서 값이 많이 싸요.
examples.en: Winter clothes are on sale now, so the prices are low.
My winter clothes have gotten too small, so I have to buy new ones.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때는 겨울옷도 꼭 챙기세요.
examples.en: Be sure to pack winter clothes too when you travel.
I haven't put away my winter clothes yet.
I dressed my child in a thick jacket as winter wear.

explain: 반대말은 '여름옷'이에요. 계절이 바뀔 때 '겨울옷 정리', '겨울옷을 꺼내다'처럼 자주 말해요. '겨울 옷'처럼 띄어 쓰지 않고 한 낱말로 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '여름옷'. When the seasons change, people often say '겨울옷 정리' or '겨울옷을 꺼내다'. It is written as one word, '겨울옷', without a space.

examples.en: It was hot, so I wore a short-sleeved T-shirt.
It's still a bit chilly for short sleeves.
Even in winter I stay in short sleeves at home.
Not the short-sleeved shirt, please give me the long-sleeved one.
The neck of this short-sleeved shirt is stretched out.

examples.ko: 안에 반소매를 입고 위에 카디건을 걸쳤어요.
examples.en: I wore a short-sleeved shirt and put a cardigan over it.

explain: 반대말은 '긴소매'예요. 일상에서는 '반팔'이라고도 많이 말해요. 옷은 '입다'와 함께 써서 '반소매를 입다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '긴소매'. In everyday talk people also say '반팔'. It goes with '입다', as in '반소매를 입다'.

en: to be on vacation; to close for a vacation

examples.en: Our school goes on vacation next week.
Our school started vacation at the end of July.
When school breaks for vacation, I'll go to my hometown.
The kids are very excited because vacation starts tomorrow.
I took photos with my friends before vacation started.
It has been a week since vacation started.

explain: 주어는 학교나 학생이고, 직장인이 쉬는 건 '방학'이 아니라 '휴가'예요. 방학이 끝나고 학교가 다시 시작하는 건 '개학하다'라서 둘이 짝이에요. '방학 동안'처럼 명사 '방학'을 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: The subject is a school or students; office workers take '휴가' (leave), not 방학. When vacation ends and school starts again, you say '개학하다', so the two are a pair. The noun appears more often, as in '방학 동안' (during the break).

en: to make a mistake; to make a slip

examples.en: It was an easy question, but I made a mistake on the exam.
Everyone makes mistakes sometimes.
It's okay to make mistakes at first.

examples.ko: 발음할 때 실수하지 않으려고 많이 연습해요.
examples.en: I practice a lot so I won't make mistakes when I pronounce words.
You must not make mistakes when calculating.
You can just fix the part where you made a mistake.

explain: '틀리다'는 답이 맞지 않다는 결과이고, '실수하다'는 아는 것을 부주의로 잘못했을 때 써요. '실수로 넘어졌어요'처럼 '실수로'를 붙이면 일부러 한 게 아니라는 말이 돼요. 정말 큰 잘못은 '잘못하다'를 써요.
explain_en: '틀리다' describes a wrong result, such as a wrong answer, while 실수하다 is slipping up on something you actually know because you weren't careful. Adding '실수로' ('by mistake') shows you didn't do it on purpose. For a real wrongdoing, use '잘못하다'.

en: to become disgusted with; to get sick of

examples.ko: 매일 같은 음식만 먹으니까 그 음식이 싫어져요.
examples.en: I eat the same food every day, so I'm getting sick of it.

examples.ko: 요즘 회사에 가는 게 점점 싫어지고 있어요.
examples.en: Lately I hate going to work more and more.

examples.ko: 친구가 거짓말을 한 뒤로 그 친구가 싫어졌어요.
examples.en: After my friend lied, I started to dislike that friend.

examples.ko: 너무 많이 먹으면 나중에 그 음식이 싫어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you eat too much, you may come to hate that food.
If studying suddenly becomes unbearable, take a short break.

examples.ko: 그 노래도 너무 자주 들으니까 싫어지더라고요.
examples.en: I heard that song so often that I got sick of it.

explain: '싫다'는 지금의 마음이고, '싫어지다'는 좋았거나 괜찮았던 것이 싫게 변했다는 뜻이에요. 반대말은 '좋아지다'예요. 같은 것을 너무 많이 해서 질릴 때는 '질리다'라고도 하는데, '싫어지다'는 음식·일뿐 아니라 사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: '싫다' is a present feeling, while '싫어지다' means something you liked or tolerated turned into something you dislike. The opposite is '좋아지다'. When you tire of something from overdoing it, '질리다' is also used, but '싫어지다' can be used for people as well as food or work.

examples.en: The cost of books is separate from tuition.

examples.ko: 이번 학기 책값이 십만 원이나 나왔어요.
examples.en: The books for this semester came to a hundred thousand won.
I borrow books from the library to save on book costs.

examples.ko: 책값 때문에 사고 싶은 책을 못 샀어요.
examples.en: I couldn't buy the book I wanted because of the price.
My older sister paid for the books for me.

examples.ko: 등록금에 책값까지 합치면 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Tuition plus book costs adds up to a lot of money.

explain: '책값이 오르다/내리다', '책값을 내다'처럼 써요. '밥값', '차비'처럼 어떤 것을 사는 데 드는 돈을 나타내는 '-값' 표현 중 하나예요. 한 단어로 붙여 쓰는 점도 알아 두세요.
explain_en: Say '책값이 오르다/내리다' (rise/fall) and '책값을 내다' (pay). It's one of the '-값' expressions for the money spent buying something, like '밥값'. Note that it is written as one word.

examples.en: I woke up at night because of the thunder.
The thunder was so loud that the child cried.
The sudden thunder startled me and I screamed.
Our puppy is afraid of the sound of thunder.
The sound of thunder is heard later than the lightning.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 천둥소리와 빗소리가 섞여 들려요.
examples.en: When it rains, thunder and rain sounds blend together.

explain: 소리를 말할 때는 '천둥소리가 나다/들리다', 현상을 말할 때는 '천둥이 치다'라고 해요. 번개는 '번개가 치다'로 같이 '치다'를 써요. 소리를 흉내 낸 말로는 '우르릉 쾅쾅'이 있어요.
explain_en: For the sound, say '천둥소리가 나다/들리다'; for the event, '천둥이 치다'. Lightning also uses '치다', as in '번개가 치다'. A word imitating the sound is '우르릉 쾅쾅'.

examples.en: The picnic was cancelled because of rain.
What do I do if the flight gets cancelled?
The reservation was cancelled, so I changed it to another day.
It is a pity that so many shows are being cancelled.

examples.ko: 갑자기 취소된 약속 때문에 시간이 생겼어요.
examples.en: The plan that suddenly got cancelled gave me free time.
I got a text saying the class will be cancelled.

explain: 일정·예약·공연처럼 이미 정해진 일이 없던 일이 될 때 써요. 내가 직접 하면 '취소하다', 다른 이유로 그렇게 되면 '취소되다'예요. 약속이 갑자기 없어지는 일은 '펑크 나다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Use it when something already planned, like a schedule, booking, or show, falls through. If you do it yourself it is 취소하다; if it happens for some other reason it is 취소되다. A plan that suddenly falls through is also called 펑크 나다 in casual speech.

examples.en: My nose tip turned red like a strawberry because of the cold.
My glasses keep sliding down to the tip of my nose.
The smell of tasty bread tickles my nose.
The cat lightly licked the tip of my nose.

examples.ko: 너무 추워서 이불을 코끝까지 덮고 잤어요.
examples.en: It was so cold that I slept with the blanket pulled up to my nose.

examples.ko: 코끝에 땀이 맺힐 만큼 열심히 뛰었어요.
examples.en: I ran so hard that sweat beaded on the tip of my nose.

explain: '코'가 얼굴의 코 전체라면 '코끝'은 맨 끝부분만 콕 집어 말해요. 추워서 빨개지거나 시릴 때, 냄새가 스칠 때처럼 코끝에서 느끼는 감각을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I got choked up while reading the letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 슬프거나 감동해서 눈물이 날 것 같을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are so sad or moved that you feel close to tears.

explain_en: While '코' is the whole nose, '코끝' points to just the very tip. It fits sensations felt at the tip, such as the nose turning red or stinging from the cold, or a smell brushing past.
